## Purpose

The **`plot_wave_height_scatter`** directory contains a self‑contained utility for generating scatter plots that compare observed wave height data against modeled wave height data (e.g., from XBeach). These visualisations help assess model performance across a range of conditions.

| File | Description |

| `plot_wave_height_scatter.py` | Defines the `WaveHeightScatterPlotter` class (or equivalent functions) that loads observed and modeled wave height datasets, aligns them in time/space, and produces Matplotlib scatter plots with optional regression lines and statistical annotations. |

## Usage Example
```python
from plot_wave_height_scatter.plot_wave_height_scatter import WaveHeightScatterPlotter

# Instantiate the plotter; it picks up default paths from helper utilities
plotter = WaveHeightScatterPlotter()
plotter.plot_scatter(
    observed_file="data/observed_wave_heights.csv",
    modeled_file="results/modeled_wave_heights.csv",
    title="Observed vs. Modeled Wave Heights",
    fname="wave_height_scatter.png",
)
```

The class (or functions) can be imported and used wherever needed (e.g., in a `main.py` script) to produce and store the scatter‑plot visualisations.

### Method Parameters
- **`observed_file`** (str): Path to the CSV (or other format) containing observed wave height measurements.
- **`modeled_file`** (str): Path to the CSV containing modeled wave height outputs.
- **`title`** (str, optional): Plot title; defaults to a generic description.
- **`fname`** (str, optional): Filename (without path) for the saved figure. If omitted, defaults to `"wave_height_scatter.png"`.
- Additional keyword arguments may control axis limits, marker styles, and statistical annotations such as R² or RMSE.
